statements.status_notes: Improper name constraint validation affecting cryptography 45.0.0 up to but not including 49.0.0, first fixed in 49.0.0. This image keeps cryptography at the version upstream GitLab CNG pins for the matching release tag, so the crypto stack matches the one GitLab validated; taking 49.0.0 would put this image three major versions ahead of CNG. The code is reachable: google-auth imports cryptography to sign service account credentials under gsutil. Resolves when CNG moves to cryptography 49.0.0 or later.

This image keeps cryptography at the version upstream GitLab CNG pins for the matching release tag, so the crypto stack matches the one GitLab validated; taking 50.0.0 would put this image four major versions ahead of CNG. The code is reachable: google-auth imports cryptography to sign service account credentials under gsutil. Resolves when CNG moves to cryptography 50.0.0 or later.

CVE alias of GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf, recorded so this document matches whichever identifier a scanner reports. The flaw is an out-of-bounds read in the OpenSSL copy that the cryptography project bundles into its prebuilt manylinux wheels, fixed in the 48.0.1 wheel. The advisory states that source installs are unaffected, because they link the system OpenSSL instead. This image builds cryptography from source, so it links the patched system OpenSSL and the vulnerable bundled copy is not present.
